numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For non-finite float inputs (inf/-inf) the Timedelta/to_timedelta construction was routed through int(item), raising a bare OverflowError that was not caught by errors="coerce" (so coercion did not yield NaT). For overflowing round-float/int inputs with a coarse unit (e.g. Timedelta(1e19, unit="s")), numpy raised a bare OverflowError that pandas did not consistently convert to OutOfBoundsTimedelta.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For infinite or overflowing float input, Timedelta/to_timedelta should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError), so that errors="coerce" returns NaT; and integer-path/np.timedelta64 overflow should be wrapped to raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta rather than a bare OverflowError.
trigger_conditions: value is a non-finite float: inf or -inf (non-finite float input routed through int(item))
value is an overflowing round float/int with a coarse unit such as Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") (numpy raises bare OverflowError)

category_specific_evidence: BUG statement: “Timedelta/to_timedelta raise bare OverflowError for inf/overflowing floats (GH#63275)”

Non-finite float input (inf/-inf) was routed through int(item), raising a bare OverflowError that errors="coerce" could not catch; expected behavior is OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError) so that errors="coerce" returns NaT

PR explanation: float("inf").is_integer() is False, so non-finite floats fall through to _numeric_to_td64ns → OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError), so coerce gives NaT; NaN is caught earlier by checknull_with_nat_and_na

Code change: in Timedelta.__new__ float branch, use item.is_integer() instead of int(item) so non-finite floats fall through to _numeric_to_td64ns; in array_to_timedelta64 similarly gate on is_integer()

Test evidence: test_round_float_overflow_unit expects Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") to raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta (match "without overflow") rather than a bare OverflowError
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may need to distinguish float infinities (np.inf/-np.inf) from NaN, since passages state NaN is caught earlier by checknull_with_nat_and_na and should not reach this float branch

provenance.value: For non-finite float inputs (inf/-inf) the Timedelta/to_timedelta construction was routed through int(item), raising a bare OverflowError that was not caught by errors="coerce" (so coercion did not yield NaT). For overflowing round-float/int inputs with a coarse unit (e.g. Timedelta(1e19, unit="s")), numpy raised a bare OverflowError that pandas did not consistently convert to OutOfBoundsTimedelta.

For infinite or overflowing float input, Timedelta/to_timedelta should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError), so that errors="coerce" returns NaT; and integer-path/np.timedelta64 overflow should be wrapped to raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta rather than a bare OverflowError.
